title: DevOps & Site Reliability
tagline: Infrastructure automation, CI/CD pipelines, container orchestration, and system observability
description: Build robust, repeatable production infrastructure from Linux kernel tuning and Docker containerization to multi-cluster Kubernetes, Terraform IaC, and full-stack OpenTelemetry observability.
prerequisites: Familiarity with at least one scripting language (Bash, Python, Go)

stages.title: Stage 1: Linux Fundamentals & Shell Automation
stages.description: Operating system internals, processes, signals, permissions, and automated scripting.

nodes.title: Linux Processes, Signals & Systemd
nodes.description: Process lifecycle (PID, fork/exec), signals (SIGTERM, SIGKILL), resource limits (cgroups), and service management via systemd unit files.
nodes.whyItMatters: Containers run as isolated Linux processes. Understanding how signals propagate is required for zero-downtime rolling deploys and graceful shutdown.
keyTakeaways: Always handle SIGTERM gracefully by completing in-flight requests within a grace period before exiting.
Use systemctl and journalctl for debugging daemon lifecycle and log streaming.
Inspect top/htop, lsof, and netstat/ss to diagnose port collisions and socket exhaustion.
nodes.interviewTips: Interviewers will ask what happens when a process receives SIGKILL vs SIGTERM, and how PID 1 reaps zombie processes.

nodes.title: Linux Networking, DNS & Firewalls
nodes.description: Routing tables, DNS resolution order (/etc/resolv.conf), iptables/nftables, and network diagnostic utilities (curl, dig, traceroute, tcpdump).
nodes.whyItMatters: Over 70% of production infrastructure outages trace back to DNS misconfigurations or routing/firewall drops between microservices.
keyTakeaways: Understand DNS record types: A, AAAA, CNAME, ALIAS, and TTL caching implications.
Use tcpdump and Wireshark to inspect packet flow when TCP handshakes time out.
Configure ulimit file descriptor and socket limits to support high concurrent connections.
nodes.interviewTips: Be prepared to walk through step-by-step how a server resolves a domain name through recursive and authoritative DNS servers.

stages.title: Stage 2: Containers & Docker Internals
stages.description: Linux namespaces, cgroups, layered union filesystems, multi-stage Docker builds, and container security.

nodes.title: Multi-Stage Docker Builds & Layer Caching
nodes.description: Crafting lightweight, minimal container images using distroless/alpine bases, ordering Dockerfile directives for optimal cache reuse, and non-root execution.
nodes.whyItMatters: Bloated 1GB+ container images slow down CI/CD deployments and increase vulnerability attack surfaces. Multi-stage builds yield slim 50MB production images.
keyTakeaways: Order Dockerfile commands from least-frequently changed (dependencies) to most-frequently changed (application source).
Never run containers as root in production; declare USER nonroot.
Use .dockerignore to avoid copying node_modules or secret credentials into image layers.
nodes.interviewTips: Expect questions on how Linux namespaces (PID, NET, MNT) and cgroups isolate containers without a virtual machine hypervisor.

stages.title: Stage 3: CI/CD & Automated Pipelines
stages.description: Automated linting, testing, artifact signing, matrix builds, and continuous deployment workflows.

nodes.title: GitHub Actions & Pipeline Automation
nodes.description: Writing declarative workflows, reusable composite actions, secret management with OIDC, and staging/production promotion gates.
nodes.whyItMatters: Manual deployments are error-prone and slow. Automated pipelines ensure every pull request is tested, scanned for CVEs, and securely deployed.

resources.title: Google Cloud OIDC with GitHub Actions

keyTakeaways: Use OpenID Connect (OIDC) instead of static long-lived cloud credentials in CI runners.
Implement pipeline caching for dependency packages to cut build times by 75%.
Enforce branch protection rules requiring passing CI checks and mandatory peer approvals.
nodes.interviewTips: Be prepared to design a complete CI/CD pipeline from PR creation to canary release in Kubernetes.

stages.title: Stage 4: Kubernetes Orchestration & GitOps
stages.description: Pods, Deployments, Services, Ingress, ConfigMaps/Secrets, Helm charts, and declarative GitOps with ArgoCD.

nodes.title: Kubernetes Control Plane & Workload Primitives
nodes.description: Control plane components (API Server, etcd, Scheduler, Controller Manager), kubelet, kube-proxy, and workload reconciliation loops.
nodes.whyItMatters: Kubernetes provides self-healing, automatic rolling updates, horizontal autoscaling (HPA), and workload portability across cloud providers.
keyTakeaways: Always define CPU and memory resource requests and limits to prevent noisy neighbor evictions.
Configure liveness and readiness probes properly to avoid routing traffic to unready pods.
Use GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux) to ensure cluster state reconciles directly with Git commits.
nodes.interviewTips: Interviewers will ask about the difference between readiness and liveness probes, and what happens when an etcd node fails.
